title: The kernel engineering system: guards, ratchets, SPEC, tests
summary: The engineering system is strong. The kernel has 636 assembly-time assertions (114 in kernel.asm, 522 in the .inc files). Budgets are derived from a stated KB rule. t_api_abi checks the API table against the emitted bytes. The ABI lock records a written reason for every fingerprint move. A dozen former prose rules are now gates (toast length, transparent text, .vga doors, module drops, movable claims, mega-only code). The weak half is what is still prose, and it fails in three repeatable shapes: running counts, hand copies of code, and section numbers that resolve to the wrong section. None of the three is gated, and each is wrong in the parts of SPEC.md a newcomer reads first (§1, §3, §4, §15-§17, §20.3). For example, checkdocs only proves a § number exists, so six citations of the greying standard point at ArtfulType's §46 and pass. The fast tier's admission rules are well argued but broken by about 17 one-package rows: the tier went from 37 to 76 rows, and the CPU budget, the only enforcement, absorbs the growth. This review's own in-progress reports currently make checkdocs, and so `make`, fail on this branch. Every fix is host-side tooling or text and costs 0 kernel bytes.

strengths.title: The assembler is the first gate
strengths.why: Content rules are enforced at the line that breaks them, at zero runtime cost: TOASTSTR length, section-checked macros through __?SECT?__, MODFP refusing an out-of-order or zero-entry module block, and osapi_sys_kb's parts required to sum to what they measure. This is GEOS Esp's convention-aware assembler done with NASM's preprocessor.

strengths.title: Budgets are derived, not chosen
strengths.why: The only decision left is the KB figure, so no budget can quietly drift. KERN_KNOB keeps knob builds out of guard 1 and says why. budget-check ends the grace on all four budgeted kernels.

strengths.title: Facts flow out of the assembler
strengths.why: The %warning ks: line hands kernsize the ladder the kernel actually has, and os88sym refuses any map that is not byte-identical, so Python does not re-derive the layout.

strengths.title: t_api_abi reads the binary
strengths.why: It decodes every cell shape out of kernel.bin and resolves each one's target. All 78 OSAPI name/number pairs in SPEC.md, CLAUDE.md, KERNEL-MEMORY.md, TESTING.md and the SDK agree today.

strengths.title: The ABI lock makes a bump a sentence
strengths.why: Each fingerprint move carries a recorded decision. The fingerprint reads code plus each OSAPI_* contract comment, not prose, so it is neither noisy nor blind.
strengths.evidence: tools/abilock.py docstring and surface(); tools/abi.lock.json history

strengths.title: Self-maintaining mirrors
strengths.why: t_mirror compares every name defined in more than one file, so a newly mirrored constant is covered without anyone remembering to add it. The lesson it records (a hand-written half makes a hand-written check) is reusable.

strengths.title: checkdocs learns from its own misses
strengths.why: It now catches duplicate headings, three-digit sections, document-qualified citations, committed conflict markers and transparent-text totals (with historical pairs). The INDEX is generated and checked. No OS project of the era gated its own documentation.

strengths.title: Small harness, actionable failures
strengths.why: check() never raises, prints want/got and the first differing offset, and why= is a habit. A gate that fails a year later can still be acted on.

strengths.title: The tier policy asks the right questions
strengths.why: Two questions decide tiers: 'is it worth having to somebody who did not touch this?' and 'did you obviously break the OS?'. The budget is charged in CPU, not wall clock, so a busy box does not fail a green tier.

findings.title: The branch's committed review reports fail checkdocs, so `make` fails; dated directories are held to today's headings
findings.detail: checkdocs on 4f0da91 reports 6 problems, all in committed review reports. checkdocs is all's first prerequisite, so `make` on the-big-review stops before building a floppy. Several of the problems are reports quoting a bad citation as evidence. The systemic half: docs/README.md says reports and history are not maintained, yet checkdocs fails on them. SITES_HIST exists to work around exactly this contradiction.
findings.recommendation: Fix the six lines now: write a quoted bad citation without its §/'SPEC.md ' prefix. Then have checkdocs print problems in docs/reports/, docs/history/ (and possibly docs/plans/completed/) as warn: lines, and keep failing everywhere else.
findings.verify_note: Re-ran tools/checkdocs.py: 6 problems, all in docs/reports/big-review-2026-11-08/areas/ (gfx.md:22, input.md:113, memory.md:132, ui.md:16 x2, video.md:773); Makefile:2425 `all: checkdocs ...`. They are this review's own in-progress reports, so the immediate half is fixed as part of assembling the review; the systemic half (docs/README.md says reports are not maintained, yet checkdocs fails on them; SITES_HIST is the workaround) stands.

findings.title: A citation that resolves to the WRONG section passes: six §46 cites mean §47
findings.detail: The preamble says renumbering is refused because checkdocs cannot catch a citation that resolves to something else. That class is already live without any renumbering. The greying standard is §47, but six SPEC.md lines cite §46 (ArtfulType), including hard rule 8, which binds packages.
findings.recommendation: Fix the six. Add a heading-drift check: compare SPEC.md's {number: title} map at the merge-base (one git show) with HEAD. Fail when a number's title changes or a title's number changes, and list every citation of the old number. Optionally, also check a parenthesised title word after a citation.
findings.prior_art: Inside Macintosh and the NT design workbook cited by chapter NAME, which cannot resolve to the wrong section.
findings.verify_note: All six cites (SPEC.md 161, 26453, 26463, 26555, 55757, 76640) say §46; §46 is ArtfulType (94991), the greying standard is §47 (96478). Doc fixes below. Note text.json's rewrite of the 26453 sentence keeps §46; this area's fix is written so it applies either way.

findings.title: SPEC.md's hand copies of code are ungated and wrong
findings.detail: Wrong today: §3 has KERNEL_SEG 0x0800 (it is 0x0060), KERN_BUDGET 74240, STK0_SIZE 1024 (512) and VIEW_KB 3 (1 or 2). §15.1 reproduces guard 1 without KERN_GRACE, the mega arm or the KERN_KNOB skip, reproduces guard 5 without BOOT2_PAD, and quotes 86,528 bytes. §62.9.1 gives DSV_SIZE as 26/28 (it is 36). Of 182 literal 'NAME equ N' lines in SPEC code fences whose name the tree defines, 4 disagree, so a gate would be nearly clean on day one.
findings.recommendation: Have t_mirror read SPEC.md's fenced nasm blocks, skipping those marked as history. Better: generate §3 and §15.1 between markers, the way the kernsize baseline block is generated.
findings.verify_note: §3: KERNEL_SEG 0x0800 (code 0x0060, kernel.asm:27), KERN_BUDGET 74240 (derived 100,864/64,000/68,096, 1446-1455), STK0_SIZE 1024 (512, 1568), VIEW_KB 3 (1 / 2 on kern_small, 1622/1628). §15.1 fence lacks KERN_GRACE, the mega arm, the KERN_KNOB skip and BOOT2_PAD; prose says 86,528. DSV_SIZE 26/28 vs 36 (driver.inc:557). The 182/4 count is not re-checked. boot.json already fixes the KERNEL_SEG, KERN_BUDGET and STK0_SIZE lines, so they are not repeated here.

findings.title: SPEC's front matter describes retired designs as current
findings.detail: §1 rule 2 gives the wrong KERNEL_SEG and LOW_SEG and says 'no far code and no second code segment', but .cold is far and has 363 far-call sites. §1 rule 4 says 'four sections' (about 30 exist) and that .bss is last (the sentinel block is). §33 says 'cold code is ordinary code, near called'. §4 lists a splash entry at 0x0008 (that address is free) and claims the table covers all of kernel/ (35 of 74 files are missing). §17 describes the File + Special menus, built-in Timers, segment 0x0800 and QEMU.
evidence: SPEC.md:4092, 4132; ls kernel/ = 74 files, 35 absent from the table
findings.recommendation: Rewrite §1-§4 and §15-§17 as a short current front matter: one paragraph per rule plus the gate that enforces it. Move the retired narrative to docs/history/. Gate §4 so every kernel/*.inc must appear in its table.
findings.prior_art: Inside Macintosh IV-VI marked what they superseded instead of rewriting history into the current chapter.
findings.verify_note: Mostly confirmed: §1 rule 2 (wrong segments, 'no far code' while 380 `call COLD_SEG:` + 22 COLDCALL sites exist), §1 rule 4 (garbled 'Two further sections ... : and `.lowbss`'; ~30 sections; the sentinel block, not .bss, is last), §33 'cold code is ordinary code, near called', §4's splash entry at 0x0008 and 35 of 74 kernel/ files without a row, §17 (logo+File+Special menus, segment 0x0800). REFUTED part: §16's `make bench` exists (Makefile:13760 `bench: $(BUILD)/bench.img $(BUILD)/bench360.img`, rules at 14509/14517).

findings.title: Two copies of the slot contracts, disagreeing in both directions
findings.detail: The SDK %define comments are fingerprinted. SPEC §20.3's 37-entry contract block is read by no tool. SND_PLAY is stale in SPEC (already listed); FULLSCREEN is stale in the SDK, which says BX is used on enter and only enter refuses, while the code binds BX on exit too and refuses either verb when another window holds the screen.
findings.recommendation: Keep the SDK as the single copy. Delete or generate §20.3's block, and fix the FULLSCREEN comment with abilock --update (no bump).
findings.prior_art: windows.h and the OS/2 .INC were the reference and the manuals rendered them; Inside Macintosh's per-chapter Summary was the one listing.
findings.verify_note: apps/os88api.inc:892-897 says BX on enter only and 'enter refused'; kernel/wm.inc:4287-4313 binds BX on exit and one latch test refuses either verb. SND_PLAY half is already in ABI-BREAK-LIST §11 and abi.json fixes SPEC's copy. The SDK comment fix needs `abilock.py --update` (no bump) in the same commit, since the fingerprint reads contract comments.

findings.title: Running counts in contract prose rot
findings.detail: The §20.3 ledger says 1,253 bytes, ending at 0x04F5; the table is 1,259 bytes, ends at 0x04FB, and OSAPI_VOL_CHECK is the 119th rare cell. 'The fifteen' inline cells heads a table of 19 rows. 'TWELVE LABELS' covers 20 sections. TESTING.md says 37/43/10/907 rows; the registry has 76/14/1944. WRITING-TESTS says five plus five full rows; there are 14. The Makefile says ~2s. CLAUDE.md says PERFORMANCE.md is 6,553 lines (it is 15,235); os88index says SPEC is 67k lines (245k). checkdocs already gates exactly one count (textsites). The OSAPI_TABLE_LEN guard is a hand tally that t_api_abi supersedes.
findings.recommendation: Generalise SITES/SITES_HIST into a COUNTS table of (regex, live computer, historical pairs). Feed it tier counts from suite.rows(), the table length and end from kernel.map, the inline-cell count and the kernel file count. Adopt a convention: a prose count either carries its moment or is not written. Derive or drop the OSAPI_TABLE_LEN tally.
findings.verify_note: Checked: table guard 44*8+11*7+119*6+... = 0x04EB = 1,259 bytes (kernel.asm:4494-4495); 'The fifteen' heads 19 rows; sentinel block checks 20 sections under 'TWELVE LABELS'; registry fast 76 / full 14 / soak 1,944 vs TESTING.md 37/43/10/907 and WRITING-TESTS 'five' + 'five'; Makefile 'all is 1,800 lines down' (it is at 2425) and '~2s'; PERFORMANCE.md 15,235 lines vs 6,553; SPEC.md 245,112 vs ~67,000. The 0x04F5 line is fixed by abi.json, not here.

findings.title: Tier admission rules are prose and are broken by about 17 fast rows and 4 full rows
findings.detail: WRITING-TESTS 2.1 says one-package, driver or tool rows are soak, with two named exceptions. Fast nonetheless carries WIN16's five, sheetfmtlib, isotronclean, lemdat, wrsim, x3xttab, stik, stikcard, romtool, catdisk, installabi, brcapacity-fixtures and arcprebuilt-stamp (about 14 declared seconds), plus chromesites, which is kernel-internal. Full has 14 rows against 10 documented; noovl is an unlisted owner ratchet, and w16censall, knobself and khpknobs break 2.2's rules. The only enforcement is the 30s CPU charge, so fast grew from 37 to 76 rows (56.9s declared) unnoticed.
findings.recommendation: Add Row(family=boundary|rules|artifacts|tree) or owner='<word, date>'. t_registry fails any fast or full row that has neither. Generate the family tables in suite.py, TESTING.md and WRITING-TESTS from the registry. Then the owner moves or exempts each row.
findings.verify_note: Confirmed for fast: 76 rows / 56.85s declared vs the 30s CPU budget, and the 17 one-package rows plus chromesites carry no owner exemption in their why= text. Corrected for full: of the four rows WRITING-TESTS does not list, noovl IS an owner ratchet ('FULL and not fast because the owner asked for it there', suite.py:2453); the three that break 2.2 are w16censall, knobself AND khpknobs (knob builds).

findings.title: Basename collisions silently disable citation checks
findings.detail: docs/README.md's 'no shared basename' rule is ungated, and 29 basenames are shared. The stems dict keeps the last path. So `LESSONS.md §3` in two skills resolves to vga-face/LESSONS.md, which numbers no headings, and is skipped as uncheckable, although the file it means numbers six.
evidence: git ls-files: README.md x27, BRIEF.md x11, SKILL.md x10, LESSONS.md x8
findings.recommendation: Resolve a qualifier first in the citing file's own directory, and by basename only when it is unique. Fail an ambiguous qualifier and name the candidates.
findings.verify_note: Confirmed mechanism (checkdocs.py:204 stems dict keeps the last path; vga-face/LESSONS.md has 0 numbered headings while refresh-stale-pr's has 6 and review-fork-pr's 13). Count corrected: 29 shared basenames today, some from this review's own areas/*.md.

findings.title: checkdocs does not read .c, .h, .txt or .sh
findings.detail: Unchecked: 1,579 citations in .c, 138 in .h and 205 in .txt (including the ratchet registries' reasons). One is known broken: pmc_menu.c:121 cites SPEC.md section 91.14, and §91 has no subsections. apps/c64/*.c writes 32 bare § citations meaning C64-SPEC, against the rule that a bare § means SPEC.md.
findings.recommendation: Add c/h/txt/sh to the scan, qualify the C64 citations and fix pmc_menu.c.
findings.verify_note: checkdocs.py scans md/inc/asm/py and Makefile only. pmc_menu.c:121 cites SPEC.md 91.14 and §91 (170017) has no numbered subsection; apps/c64/*.c carry ~60 bare § cites meaning C64-SPEC (counts not re-derived exactly).

findings.title: AGENTS.md has diverged from CLAUDE.md by 726 lines
findings.detail: Both files say they carry the same guidance and differ only in title and intro. After line 12, 726 lines differ (786 against 1,370 lines). A Codex session reads older rules.
findings.recommendation: Generate AGENTS.md from CLAUDE.md with a substitution table for the intro and tool names, and check it in checkdocs the way the index is checked.
findings.verify_note: CLAUDE.md 1,370 lines vs AGENTS.md 786; `diff` after line 12 prints 726 changed lines; both files' line 5 says they carry the same guidance.

findings.title: The C SDK's constants and thunks are outside both t_mirror and the ABI lock
findings.detail: t_mirror's C list covers four emulator .c files and not os88.h, whose OS88_ prefix would defeat name pairing anyway. abilock fingerprints os88api.inc and os88drv.inc only. os88.h has 80 numeric defines; 57 pair with SDK names and all agree today.
findings.recommendation: Add os88.h to t_mirror with a prefix map, and add os88.h and os88thunk.asm to PKG_FMT's fingerprint files.
findings.prior_art: Microsoft H2INC generated MASM includes from C headers so the two could not disagree.
findings.verify_note: t_mirror CDEF lists only the four emulator .c files (t_mirror.py:181-183); abilock GUARDS fingerprints os88api.inc and os88drv.inc only. 57/80 agreement not re-counted.

findings.title: Section switch-back is gated only for nobits sections
findings.detail: With -w+error, NASM only refuses a nobits section left open. A progbits section left open is silent. shutdown.inc ends in .modu by design, because ctrl.inc includes it inside .modu. The sentinel block covers 20 sections but not .modx/.mods/.modfs/.vga/.cfx; for an exact start= successor NASM itself fails with a section overlap (verified), so only padded gaps need a sentinel.
findings.recommendation: Add a host check that each kernel .inc's last section directive equals the section active at its %include (or .text), with an exemption list.
findings.verify_note: kernel/shutdown.inc ends in .modu (its one section line, :5), included at ctrl.inc:1038 inside .modu (1021); no other kernel .inc ends outside .text. The sentinel block omits .vga, .cfx, .modx, .mods, .modfs. NASM overlap behaviour not re-tested.

findings.title: Ratchets are exact-match registers, not one-way; 21 bespoke parsers
findings.detail: The gates force registry == tree in both directions, but a new line raising a count passes with any reason. Direction is held only by review.
findings.recommendation: Write a shared tests/unit/ratchet.py (parse, require a reason, compare with the tree) and have it print a warn: line when a registry total rises against the merge-base. A candidate new registry: the 27 bare sti in kernel/.

findings.title: Gates regex NASM source for facts the assembler already emits
findings.detail: t_kernbudget finds three KERN_BUDGET arms by position and evaluates one expression shape, although the ks: line already prints budget=. A source reformat breaks such gates even when nothing semantic changed.
findings.recommendation: Read derived facts from the ks:/ksm: lines or kernel.map. Keep source regexes for rules that are about the source itself.
findings.verify_note: t_kernbudget.py:72-98 locates three `KERN_BUDGET equ` arms by position and accepts one expression shape; the ks: line already reports budget.

findings.title: The whole-soak permission refusal is bypassed by -k '*'
findings.detail: Both runners test only `not a.k`, so any glob that matches everything runs all 1,944 rows without --user-asked.
findings.recommendation: Also refuse when the selection covers more than ~90% of the tier.
findings.verify_note: os88test.py:1318 and os88soak.py:1050 refuse only on `not a.k`; -k is fnmatch (os88test.py:1338), so -k '*' selects all 1,944 soak rows without --user-asked.

findings.title: builds= is judged per script, not per mode
findings.detail: brcapacity-fixtures is a fast row that runs no make. It carries builds=True only because the script runs make in other modes, so the row leaves the parallel lane and its flag says something false.
findings.recommendation: Move the row to soak (it is a one-package row), or key t_registry's make test on the row's argv.
findings.verify_note: The row's own why= says 'builds=True only because the registry reads tests/brcapacity.py for `make`; the --fixtures mode runs no make'.

findings.title: Guards are cited by unstable, out-of-order numbers
findings.detail: In file order the guards are numbered 1, 2, 2d, 3, 3b, 4, 6, 7, 6b, 4b, 5, 5b, 5c. SPEC §3 refers to a 'guard 8', and docs cite guards by number.
findings.recommendation: Give each guard a stable tag in its %error text (e.g. [G-BUDGET]) and cite the tags.
findings.verify_note: File order is 1, 2, 2d, 3, 3b, 4, 6, 7, 6b, 4b, 5, 5b, 5c (kernel.asm:9438-9715); no guard 8 exists, but SPEC §3 cites 'guard 8'.

findings.title: SPEC.md is two documents: 56% of it is package design notes
findings.detail: 245,112 lines and 5,212 numbered headings. 137,687 lines are package sections and 107,389 kernel/system. 239 headings are out of numeric order among their siblings. The binding kernel contract is a minority of the document that claims to be it.
findings.recommendation: Move each package section into <PKG>-SPEC.md, keeping its numbers. This is a mechanical citation rewrite that checkdocs already resolves. SPEC.md keeps the kernel, the ABI and cross-package standards. Add a generated number-to-line TOC to INDEX.
findings.prior_art: Inside Macintosh had a chapter per manager; Minix kept its contract small enough to print beside the code.
findings.verify_note: SPEC.md is 245,112 lines with 129 top-level sections; '### 22.15' (52774) precedes '### 22.6' (53330). The 56% split is not re-measured.

findings.title: Machine-readable routine contracts (register discipline is ungated)
findings.detail: Hard rule 3 has no gate; the stack walker checks balance, not clobbers. The kernel already has 1,476 '; out:' and 804 '; clobbers:' header lines, which nothing parses, and they drift: wm_content's header says W_X+1 but the routine returns W_X for a flush-left window.
findings.recommendation: Fix a header grammar (in/out/clobbers/flags/lock). Generate an autodoc-style routine reference from it. Add a conservative report-only checker that flags a register written but neither listed in out:/clobbers: nor saved and restored.
findings.prior_art: GEOS PASS:/RETURN:/DESTROYED: headers; MASM PROC USES; AmigaOS autodocs.
findings.verify_note: wm_content's header (wm.inc:5697) says W_X+1 but `call wm_flush / jc .full` returns W_X for a flush-left window; ~1,480 '; out:' and ~900 clobbers lines exist and nothing parses them.

findings.title: A checked build at the API boundary
findings.detail: Many SDK contracts are preconditions that can be checked at runtime: the gfx lock held, BX is the caller's window, UI task only, DF=0. Nothing checks them while the system runs.
evidence: apps/os88api.inc contract comments ('caller holds the gfx lock', 'a window of YOURS')
findings.recommendation: Add a CHECKED=1 knob that asserts those preconditions in the SLOT/RSLOT dispatch for the cells whose contract names them, reporting through the debug registry (§57). Add a soak row that drives packages under it.
findings.prior_art: Windows 3.1 debug KERNEL parameter validation; NT checked build.

findings.title: The Makefile is one 20,872-line file, 53% comments
findings.detail: 11,044 of the lines are comments and there is one include. The incident narratives are valuable, but each is a claim that rots in place.
findings.recommendation: Split by subject into mk/*.mk, following the apps/cc/Makefile.inc precedent. Move long narratives to the doc that owns each subject and leave a pointer.
findings.verify_note: Makefile is 20,872 lines with ~11,070 comment lines; the only include is apps/cc/Makefile.inc (10105).

doc_fixes.old_text:
Cold code is ordinary code, near
called like everything else. If the image has to shrink it shrinks by doing
less or doing it smaller, not by moving it somewhere the accounting cannot
see.
doc_fixes.new_text:
Cold code goes in `.cold` (§2.6),
a code segment of its own entered by far calls, and it is still RESIDENT:
`.cold` relieves the 64KB window and nothing else. If the footprint has to
shrink it shrinks by doing less or doing it smaller, or by becoming an
on-demand module (§2.8), not by moving it somewhere the accounting cannot
see.
doc_fixes.why: kernel/kernel.asm:2159 section .cold at COLD_SEG; 380 `call COLD_SEG:` and 22 COLDCALL sites in kernel/; far entries end in retf (SPEC 2.6.1)
